canonical.title: Iterative Postorder Traversal of Binary Tree

narrative.title: The Return-Visit Warranty Clerk
narrative.scenario: A warranty clerk walks a dealership's branch chart loop-only: no recursive paperwork chains permitted. She parks nodes on her desk pile while sliding left, but a station may only be signed off once its right branch is either empty or already stamped — she keeps a seen-it ledger to tell the difference. If the right branch still needs work, it goes on the pile and the loop slides left through it first.
narrative.inputFormat: The root of a binary tree given as a level-order array where null marks a missing child.
narrative.outputFormat: Return an array of node values in postorder, produced without recursion.
constraints: No recursive calls allowed — the traversal must run on an explicit stack

testCases.explanation: Children always land before their parents; the root closes the log.
With no right branch pending, the lone node is stamped on the first peek.

hintLevels: Level 1: Postorder is the hardest to iterate because a node can be visited twice — once to scout its right wing, once to record it.
Level 2: Peek the stack top; record-and-pop only when its right subtree is null or already stamped in a visited set.
Level 3: Otherwise push the right child and re-slide left through it — every node still gets pushed and popped exactly once.
